_comment: Org baseline for Claude Code hooks. Guardrails are always-on; modules are opt-in. 'enforcement' is the global posture: 'block' (hooks fail the tool call) or 'warn' (hooks advise only). The installer copies this file to a target repo's .claude/baseline.config.json only if one is not already present, so local customizations are never clobbered.
_malformedConfigRationale: If this file EXISTS but cannot be read as a JSON object (not valid JSON, not UTF-8/16/32 text, or a top level that is not an object), every lookup would return its built-in default: module gating would read false (scope-guard, config-guard and the rest would quietly stop), and commandGuard.extraPatterns would disappear while command-guard kept reporting success. So every wired hook tests bcl_config_malformed BEFORE its enabled-gate. command-guard, scope-guard, the PostToolUse dispatcher and config-guard route it through bcl_failclosed_exit, which on such a file reads the default posture and failClosed and so exits 2 ('control could not run', naming the file and the parse error), not a silent pass. tracker-reminder is a Stop hook, where exit 2 would keep Claude working, so it shows the same message and exits 0. Every guarded call is then refused until a human fixes or deletes the file; Claude's edit tools are denied it. A UTF-8 byte order mark or UTF-16 text (what Windows PowerShell 5.1 writes) is read, not refused. tools/baseline-status.sh reports such a file as a finding, and install.sh warns about one it keeps. A file that is simply ABSENT is a different case and still means 'defaults apply' - that is a fresh checkout, not a degraded one.
_minClaudeCodeVersionRationale: Floor for behavior this baseline depends on: the higher of two documented minimums. v2.1.314 is the first release in which shell commands Claude starts with the Monitor tool reach Bash-matched PreToolUse hooks, so command-guard sees them; below it a Monitor command bypasses command-guard (Bash deny rules still apply). v2.1.295 added onFailure:block, which the PreToolUse guards set so that a guard that cannot start or times out blocks the call instead of letting it through; older releases do not support the key (how they treat it is unverified), and there a guard that cannot start most likely fails open. It also covers v2.1.77, where a PreToolUse hook returning 'allow' could no longer bypass a 'deny' rule, which the tamper-protection deny-list (Edit(.claude/settings.json) etc.) relies on. install.sh compares the detected 'claude --version' against this and warns (advisory, never blocks) if older. Re-confirm per release via RELEASING.md.
_baselineVersionRationale: Revision stamp for THIS baseline template (distinct from the schema 'version' integer above). install.sh copies it verbatim onto a NEW install (create path only - an existing config is never rewritten), and the same value ships in hooks/VERSION, which install.sh recopies into every repo on each run. tools/baseline-status.sh --drift compares a repo's installed .claude/hooks/baseline/VERSION against this value to surface repos on an old baseline. Bump this AND hooks/VERSION together on release (see RELEASING.md); tests/run.sh asserts the two match.
_autoFormatRationale: autoFormat ships DISABLED, unlike the other guardrail. It is the one hook in this baseline that EXECUTES code the target repository supplies: after cd'ing to the repo root it runs ./node_modules/.bin/prettier and ./node_modules/.bin/eslint when present - repo-controlled binaries - honouring repo-controlled prettier.config.js / eslint.config.js and their plugins, and 'dotnet format' additionally builds the project. Cloning a repo and letting an agent touch one file would then be enough to run whatever that repo planted, which is the same primitive as the repo-defined-hook auto-execution the baseline exists to contain. Enabling it is a deliberate trade for a repo whose toolchain you trust: set guardrails.autoFormat.enabled true here. The hook reads that key with bcl_guardrail_opted_in, so ONLY a literal true in a readable config turns it on - a missing key, a missing config or an unreadable one keeps it off. Every other guardrail only inspects, so those keep the default-on gate (absent config must not mean absent enforcement).
